title: Non-blocking follow-ups from backend-trade-strategy-tagging-followups review (PR #252)
description: Non-blocking findings from the pr-reviewer pass on PR #252 (whitespace-normalization field_validator added to PositionIn.strategy), tracked here per CLAUDE.md's convention so they aren't lost once the PR merges.

checklist.step: `PositionIn._strip_and_normalize_entry_notes` and `PositionIn._strip_and_normalize_strategy` (backend/app/api/schemas.py) now have byte-for-byte identical bodies (strip; normalize a resulting empty string to None). Pydantic's `field_validator` decorator accepts multiple field names in one call (e.g. `@field_validator("entry_notes", "strategy")`), so these could be consolidated into a single validator function to avoid the duplication, rather than keeping two separately-named copies of the same four lines. Worth doing next time either validator needs to change, so the two don't silently drift apart. Non-blocking: no correctness impact today, purely a reuse/simplification cleanup.

decisions.decision: Consolidated `PositionIn._strip_and_normalize_entry_notes` and `_strip_and_normalize_strategy` (backend/app/api/schemas.py) into a single `_strip_and_normalize_optional_text` method decorated with `@field_validator("entry_notes", "strategy")`, per Pydantic's documented support for multiple field names on one validator. Chose a name describing the shared behavior (strip; normalize empty string to None) rather than keeping one of the two original field-specific names, since neither field name alone is more descriptive of a validator that now applies to both. No behavior, schema, or OpenAPI-shape change -- verified `backend/openapi.json` is byte-identical after `python scripts/export_openapi.py`, and the full backend test suite (1144 tests, including the entry_notes/strategy whitespace/merge regression tests in test_portfolio_positions.py) still passes.
decisions.rationale: The two validators were byte-for-byte identical in body, differing only in decorated field and function name -- exactly the drift risk this follow-up task called out. Pydantic v2's field_validator explicitly supports multiple field names in one decorator call, so a single shared validator is the straightforward fix with no alternative approach worth considering.

review.notes: Full review: backend suite green (1144 passed, 99.95% coverage vs 90% gate), ruff/mypy/profit-target-wording-guard clean, frontend untouched so skipped. Task board: checklist item has a proper decisions entry (decision + rationale); scripts/validate_tasks.py reports 0 violations. No blocking or non-blocking findings.
